- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is rising.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast.
- If sentiment history shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.5+), model often fails to capture full rally; increase forecast by 1–3% beyond trendline.
- When sentiment is flat or mildly negative, model tends to lag; forecast should be 1–2 days ahead of true price if sentiment is stable.
